text:
Marco: FYI, after the continuous-batcher queue-rebalance change deployed last night we're seeing a recurring KV cache "thump" on prod (cluster-eu-1). p95 token latency bumped ~120ms for small interactive requests.

Priya: Noted. Is it correlated with any specific kernel selection flips?

Marco: Early signal looks like kernel-affinity oscillation when batch shapes shift rapidly. Router logs show repeated kernel fallback to slow-path every ~30s. Sample from router: `router: prefer_kernel=vulkan_fast -> fallback=cuda_generic (latency 110ms)`

Dan: Can you paste the batching heuristic config that rolled out? I want to check token_budget and queue_rebalance thresholds.

Marco: Rolled config snippet (from deploy):
```
continuous_batcher:
  token_budget_target: 48
  queue_rebalance:
    window_ms: 250
    threshold_pct: 0.35
  prefer_small_batch_kernels: true
```

Priya: token_budget_target 48 is lower than previous 64, and queue window got shorter. That could increase churn for tiny requests and blow KV cache locality.

Alice: Profiling dump (30s span) from a host exhibiting the thump:
```
2026-06-10T03:12:01Z kernel_switch_count=42
2026-06-10T03:12:01Z avg_batch_size=2.1
2026-06-10T03:12:01Z kv_cache_miss_rate=0.27
2026-06-10T03:12:01Z p50_token_latency=12ms p95_token_latency=138ms
```

Nora: kv_cache_miss_rate 27% is huge compared to norm ~6-8%. If batches are too small and switching kernels, the KV cache entries get evicted or not reused.

Dan: Agreed. Hypothesis: queue-rebalance window shrink + lower token budget causes rapid micro-batching; runtime flips kernel affinity for small batches -> different memory footprint -> KV thrash.

Marco: Quick mitigation suggestion: revert window_ms to 400 and token_budget_target to 64 for the next patch. Also add a short cooldown on kernel affinity flips (e.g., min_stable_window_ms: 2000).

Priya: Can we run an A/B on a single AZ with the revert? I'll run a perf test and compare router/kcache metrics.

infra-bot: deploy requested by @Priya: rolling update continuous-batcher-config v2 -> v1-revert to cluster-eu-1 (canary). ETA 3m. :gear:

Marco: Thanks. While canary runs, please capture `kb-profile` (kernel-bind profile) and `kv-cache-stats` every 10s. Also enable debug tracing for kernel selection for 60s.

Alice: Ran lightweight collect; attaching excerpt of kb-profile diff between bad and revert canary: `kb_hotset_shift=+0.48, affinity_flip_rate=-0.82`. Revert reduced flips and kv miss rate dropped to ~9%. p95 latency returned to baseline.

Dan: That aligns. We should tune continuous-batcher to bias towards kernel stability when kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.15. New rule: if kv miss > 0.15, increase token_budget_target by 50% for that route and extend queue window by 100ms.

Nora: Can we add a short-term alert on kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.15 for any host for >60s? That would catch regressions faster.

Marco: I'll file a follow-up RFC for policy change and a permanent canary gating check. For now we keep revert and monitor for 30m.

Priya: Monitoring looks good so far. p95 back down, kernel_flip_count stable. Will keep an eye and post a summary after 30m. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy succeeded: canary completed, no rollback triggered.

Marco: Great work. Action items: 1) RFC for adaptive token_budget on kv miss, 2) implement kernel-affinity cooldown, 3) add kv miss alert. I'll create JIRAs.

Alice: I'll include the profiling traces and sample logs in the ticket.

Dan: Thanks team. Short postmortem if revert doesn't hold.

Marco: Closing thread for now — please add any follow-ups in the ticket.
